name: Albion
axesStatus: Illustrative equal axes at a diameter estimated from brightness with an assumed albedo of 0.14; not measured.
credit: JPL Small-Body Database absolute magnitude H = 7.18 for 15760 Albion (1992 QB1); diameter estimated by cssEarth with the 0.14 median albedo of cold classical objects from Vilenius et al. (2014), Astronomy & Astrophysics 564, A35
shapeMeaning: Illustrative sphere at 130.2 km, estimated from JPL's absolute magnitude H = 7.18 with an assumed albedo of 0.14, the median Vilenius et al. (2014) report for cold classical objects. The size is not measured.
orientationMeaning: Illustrative ICRF north pole, arbitrary prime meridian and phase; no spin pole is published.
surfaceMeaning: Unmapped surface: the standard grid is a coordinate aid, not observed colour or terrain.
introduction: Albion, found in 1992 as 1992 QB1, was the first Kuiper belt object discovered after Pluto and Charon.
card: The first Kuiper belt object found after Pluto.
datasetSummary: A sphere at about 130.2 km, estimated from brightness with an assumed albedo.
